I chose Chooi Leng after attending her workshop, where she appeared friendly and knowledgeable. However, this decision has ultimately proved to be a costly and time-consuming experience without a usable outcome. Based on our experience, I would not recommend her service.

Having recently moved to the UK, I relied on her to guide us through what was a completely new process. Our garden is around one acre, and we made it clear from the outset that our budget was approximately £20,000 (with limited flexibility) — this was precisely why we engaged a designer.

However, our experience raised several concerns:

* Budget misalignment: The design led to contractor quotes starting from £60,000, far exceeding our stated budget
* Inaccurate measurements: Patio dimensions in the design were later found to be incorrect when reviewed by the contractor
* Existing planting ignored: Mature camellias and hydrangeas around the house were effectively removed in the design, rather than incorporated
* Lack of accountability: Requests to revise the layout based on correct measurements and existing conditions were declined
* Questionable value: A revised planting scheme was offered only if we determined ourselves which plants to retain, and within the existing layout — leaving it unclear what the designer’s role was intended to be in this process

Having paid over £3,000 in design fees, we are now left re-measuring the garden and reassessing planting ourselves.

Overall, this was not a practical or buildable design, and did not provide the guidance we expected from a professional service.

WOW. If you’re planning a walk or cycle along the Monsal Trail and thinking of stopping here, you may want to pack your own food and drink (and perhaps your own toilet paper).

I fully appreciate the cost‑of‑living pressures everyone is under, but I really don’t expect to be paying London prices at a small rural café in the middle of the Peak District.

I can’t remember the exact breakdown (other than my own when I saw the bill), but roughly:

• 2 Americanos – around £4.40 each (nice coffee)
• 1 sausage roll – around £5.10 (average)
• 1 Bakewell slice – around £4.15 (also average)
Grand total: £18.05.

Yes, I could have walked away, but it was around midday, we were a few miles from the nearest alternative, and I was out with my daughter with minimal rations. So I paid it, chalked it up to experience, and moved on.

Unfortunately, the visit was capped off by the temporary toilets, which were genuinely unpleasant and close to unusable. I understand the café doesn’t own them, but if you’re directing customers to them because your own facilities are out of action, there’s at least some responsibility to ensure they’re checked, reported, or simply marked as closed if they’re not fit for use.

I’ve been visiting the Peaks for over 40 years, and one of the things I’ve always loved is the quality, value, and pride shown by rural cafés. It’s usually a pleasure to support them. Sadly, not on this occasion. A look at their website suggests this café is part of a chain (Blueberry Food), which perhaps explains the pricing.
But don’t just take my word for it, try it for yourself and see what you think.

The timing of system updates is poorly managed. Updates are happening during high-demand periods, which disrupts work and creates frustration. Please review your update schedule and move maintenance to times when the system is less in use

Where do I even start. On the surface, Courier Exchange is a solid platform. There’s consistent workflow, and you can make decent money… if your only expense in life is fuel.

The problem is the downsides outweigh the positives, and most of them are completely avoidable and easily fixable.

For load posters, the platform is perfect. Jobs that should realistically be priced at £1–£1.50 per mile are regularly sold for around 60p per mile, while their end customer is being charged £2+ per mile. The margins are huge, which explains the constant flow of work. It works brilliantly for them, just not for the drivers actually doing the job.

Even with fuel costs where they are, rates haven’t adjusted. I understand companies don’t want to lose customers, but there still needs to be a baseline level of fairness.

Where CX falls short is failing to protect drivers. There’s nothing in place to ensure fair rates, so it turns into a bidding war, a race to the bottom. Bust fools. Drivers undercut each other just to win work, and many companies bidding on jobs are running hourly-paid drivers. That means they can afford to bid extremely low just to keep their driver moving, even if the job itself is barely profitable. It makes sense from a business perspective, but it destroys the market for everyone else.

This could be addressed with simple rules or safeguards around pricing. At the moment, there’s nothing.

Then there are payment terms. You secure a job at a decent rate, only to find 45 days end of month, or even 60-day terms. Meanwhile, fuel has already been paid for. And you have to wait 45-60 days for this money to come in…  Realistically, you need a cash float of around £5,000 just to stay operational while waiting to be paid, the money you’re entitled to, the money YOU worked for. It’s a joke.

So now what happens, drivers look for solutions like invoice factoring to maintain cash flow. BUT GUESS WHAT, CX has banned factoring altogether. Instead, they’ve introduced “SmartPay” and “Early Pay”, which only work if the load poster enables it, and 80%  don’t have it on😂

Okay let’s say it is available, the fees range from 15–25%. At that point, a large portion of your profit is gone instantly. It’s ridiculous.

This is another self-inflicted issue. CX could easily allow factoring again or introduce a fair, capped fee structure and make early payment standard across the platform without greedy fees. Instead, drivers are left with limited and expensive options.

I don’t even want to comment on the platform fees themselves, which by the way continue to increase year after year, with no justification. Lyall Cresswell is rubbing his hands together at the smell of the money.

Overall, the platform has potential and clearly works well for load posters, but drivers, who are the backbone of it, are left carrying most of the risk and cost.

Courier Exchange, please address these issues.

Joining them was the worse experience ever. Very unfair and definitely not accurate on the jobs they apply to be posting each day. Their prices rise again selectively up to members. Some get massive increase some none at all. If there was a zero i would gladly put a zero.

I rarely leave reviews but this needs to be said. Courier Exchange markets itself as a neutral and professional platform, but based on my experience that simply isn’t the case. A courier company, HBC Logistics, was allowed to operate while clearly breaching multiple Courier Exchange rules. They were posting jobs, collecting bids, then diverting drivers off-platform onto their own system (SmartLM), cancelling the jobs on CX, and continuing the work externally. Even more concerning, data linked to those jobs, including driver contact details, was then used to market directly to my drivers and encourage them to leave my company and join their platform. That is completely unacceptable and raises serious data protection concerns. Courier Exchange were provided with evidence of this behaviour yet allowed both HBC Logistics and the SmartLM integration to continue operating for a prolonged period. At the same time, SmartLM was presented as a partnered or trusted integration despite clearly being linked to a competing logistics company. When issues were raised, the responses were slow, generic and focused on deflecting responsibility rather than addressing what was actually happening. This is not how a neutral marketplace should operate. If a platform allows one member to extract data, bypass the system and gain a competitive advantage, it undermines trust for everyone using it. There is a good platform underneath, but governance, enforcement and data protection standards need serious improvement. Until that happens I would advise businesses to be cautious about what data they share and how they operate on here.

I booked this massage really looking forward to feeling relaxed and “chilled” afterwards, like I usually do after a deep tissue session. I asked for a medium to hard pressure as I’ve had many deep tissue massages before and generally tolerate firm pressure well, so I do understand the difference between therapeutic discomfort and excessive force.

Unfortunately, this experience crossed that line for me. The pressure used throughout most of the session felt far beyond what was manageable. I was tensing up constantly and at points felt close to tears, and I ended up crying afterwards. I left feeling distressed rather than relaxed.

What concerned me most was the lack of check-ins or adjustment during the treatment, despite how visibly my body was reacting. The pressure was only reduced after I eventually asked for it to be softer. In my experience, a good deep tissue massage should be responsive to the client’s body rather than pushing through sustained resistance.

There is also an important distinction with deep tissue work: if pressure causes the body to tense or go into “protection mode,” it becomes counterproductive, because the therapist can no longer effectively access deeper layers of muscle tissue. That’s part of why this felt unhelpful rather than therapeutic.

For me, there is a clear difference between effective deep pressure and pain that feels overwhelming, and unfortunately this experience felt much closer to the latter.

Never again.

I strongly advise anyone considering using DP Doors & Shutters to proceed with extreme caution. My recent experience with this company was deeply disappointing and, in my opinion, completely unacceptable.

I contacted them regarding a shutter issue and booked an appointment. Before any work was carried out, I specifically asked the engineer how much the repair would cost. I was clearly told that I would only need to pay the callout charge. Based on that assurance, I agreed for the repair to go ahead. The issue itself was resolved in around 10 minutes.

However, when I later requested the invoice from the office, I was absolutely shocked to be charged a staggering £295 for what was a very quick and straightforward job. When I asked for a breakdown of the charges, I was told the bill included:

£100 travel cost
£30 “Health & Safety” charge
£15 admin fee
£100 labour charge

The figures appeared completely inflated and unjustified for the amount of work carried out. At no stage were these charges explained or agreed with me beforehand. Had I been told the true cost in advance, I would never have proceeded.

I paid the invoice simply to end the matter and avoid further stress, but I will never use this company again. I feel it is important to warn others so they do not end up in the same situation.

My advice to anyone considering this company is:

Get every quote and charge confirmed in writing before work starts.
Do not rely on verbal assurances.
Ask for a full breakdown upfront.
Be extremely careful, as additional costs may be added afterwards without clear prior agreement.

Please think twice before using this company.

I have owned a Franke Omni boiling water tap for five years and purchased replacement filters directly from Greg Rowe — the UK manufacturer behind the Franke Omni — every six months throughout that time. I was a loyal, repeat customer of both brands.

The tap failed when the ferrule on the boiling water tank hose corroded, causing a leak and rendering both the boiling and filtered water functions completely unusable. When I contacted Greg Rowe for support, I was told the hose tails are not detachable from the tap body and that my only option was to buy a completely new tap at £350 plus fitting costs.

No goodwill gesture. No acknowledgement that the ferrule design was later revised — which strongly implies this was a known failure point. No interest whatsoever in retaining a customer who had spent consistently with them for five years.

I sent a formal written complaint to Greg Rowe. No response was received.

I then contacted Franke UK directly, hoping that a brand of their standing would want to know how their customers were being treated. Their response was to refer me straight back to Greg Rowe.

The tap carries Franke's name and is sold on the strength of their reputation. When things go wrong, that responsibility cannot simply be passed back and forth between manufacturer and brand until the customer gives up.

The product failure itself was frustrating. The complete indifference shown by both Greg Rowe and Franke UK to a loyal, long-standing customer is what has brought me here. I would not buy from either again and could not recommend their after-sales support to anyone.

I’m not one to write bad reviews but feel that the cladding we purchased and installed from Envirobuild is so bad and has not lived up to any of the promises made on the website it is necessary to in this case. Having to give even one star feels wrong!

We purchased over £1500 worth of cladding last year in 2025 to cover an outside wall running to the side of a stone stairwell at the front of our house. Our landscaper installed the cladding using composite 50mm battens. It looked great for a few weeks but we started noticing it staining and did find it difficult to clean.

Now, just 12 months after installation and after one Cornish winter the problems have become much worse and we are now looking to strip it all out and will have to start again with a different material. It looks horrendous.

The cladding boards have warped, cracked and stained so badly it is difficult to comprehend after such a short space of time.

I need to measure this against the promises made on the website, which are:

"it’s designed to withstand rain, humidity, and moisture” - It has not withstood any of these.

"without rotting, warping, or splitting” - it has warped and split.

"Performs Well in Wet Conditions” - it has not. My 20 year old wooden shed is in better condition.

"Composite cladding typically lasts 25 to 30 years” - It has not lasted one year.

"Cleaning composite cladding is simple” & “best stain resistance" - it is not. I have followed the guidance to try and remove the staining several times but it will not come off. It looks terrible after 12 months in place.

"Comprehensive warranty – Warranties of up to 25 years covering structural integrity and fade and stain protection.” - so how good is the warranty?

I reported the issue with them and they stated that they can’t help and the warranty is void because our landscaper did not leave a 20mm gap at the top of the boards as per the installation guide. This implies that the issue is begin caused by a downward pressure but the boards are not pushing at the ends and the gap that was left is still clear of the adjacent material. They are swelling widthways where they lock together causing the boards to warp and split all the way along the wall. We have over a 50mm gap between the floor and the cladding where the problem is most severe.

They also said the warranty was void because we didn’t install a waterproof membrane. As the cladding is not on a wall to the house we deemed it unnecessary as the installation guide says the “membrane should be installed to protect the walls”, not the cladding. The cladding surely is meant to be weather resistant.

Other materials we installed in the garden project still all look like new. This includes Millboard decking and Cedar cladding which have resisted the weather incredibly well and are easy to clean. We really did trust that this cladding would be weather resistant and provide some longevity. It’s been a complete waste of money and the promises and warranty mean nothing.

Interestingly, we left the offcuts from our project outside and the few boards of cladding we have left are completely stained, warped and cracking while the Millboard leftovers are spotless and resistant to the weather. This is quite telling.

I have uploaded a filmed review of the cladding problems so you can find this by searching YouTube for “Envirobuild Cladding Nightmare”.

If you are considering buying this cladding please save yourself the time and money and choose a different, more suitable product. We’ve learnt the hard way and wasted a lot of money installing this. Avoid!

I had a very frustrating experience with InstallPros and I feel it’s important to warn others.

I initially looked into Starlink after a friend recommended it. Their website clearly advertised no upfront costs, with a promotional price of £25 per month for six months, rising to £35 thereafter. Based on that, I decided to make an enquiry.

After reaching out, I was contacted by InstallPros, which at first seemed like part of the same company. However, it turns out they are just a third-party installer. What shocked me was that they quoted me £700 for hardware and installation — something that directly contradicts what’s advertised on the official Starlink website.

This feels incredibly misleading. At no point was it made clear that a third party would be involved or that such a significant upfront cost could apply. It gives the impression that customers are being funneled toward expensive installation services that aren’t actually required.

In my opinion, this comes across as a rip-off, and I’d strongly advise others to double-check who they’re dealing with before agreeing to anything. Transparency is seriously lacking here.

Fidler & Pepper were our acting solicitors for both the sale and purchase. Our experience during the process was incredibly stressful and deeply frustrating and we would NOT recommend their services for the reasons below.

The process dragged from March 2025 through to September 2025 with significant and avoidable delays throughout.

Communication became a major issue. What started off well quickly deteriorated into days and often weeks without any updates, leaving us constantly chasing for basic information. Responses were reactive rather than proactive, and it was almost impossible to speak to anyone directly. Calls were repeatedly blocked by the receptionist, with callbacks rarely happening, adding to the sense of being completely unsupported during a time-sensitive transaction.

Searches were confirmed as complete on 1st May 2025, yet there was virtually no progress for at least three months. Even more concerning, critical enquiries regarding an oil leak and underpinning, issues clearly identified in the original searches, were only raised at the end of July, putting the entire chain at serious risk at a very late stage.

We were under constant pressure from the chain, with repeated threats that our buyers were close to pulling out due to the lack of progress from Fidler & Pepper. It became clear they were not only slow in responding to us, but were also ignoring communications from the buyers’ solicitors and estate agent, further escalating tensions and delays across the chain. There was certainly no sense of urgency.

Because of how long the process took, we were also at risk of losing our HSBC mortgage deal, which added significant financial pressure on top of an already difficult situation. We made a complaint which got to the escalation team, however it seemed they didn’t care about the situation at hand as there was still no movement. When it came to signing important documents, Fidler & Pepper sent legal documents as a Word document still with track changes and my name spelt incorrectly. We told them about it and the response was “just sign it, and we’ll correct it afterwards”. Shocking response from solicitors who are dealing with your legal documentation!

This lack of urgency, poor communication, and last-minute handling of key issues caused serious and unnecessary stress, not just for us but for multiple families involved.

Overall, this was an exhausting and highly stressful experience. We would not recommend Fidler & Peppers services and strongly advise those to choose their solicitors carefully and read reviews beforehand.

***Note: This review is being left in March 2026. The delay in posting is due to how stressful and, at times, traumatic the whole entire experience was, and the time it has taken to feel able to revisit it.

Wish I would have read these reviews before booking!

We booked a “17-seater” bus for my son’s birthday outing, only to discover on arrival that it actually had 16 seats - meaning one person had to stand. That alone was unacceptable and unsafe.

At the start of the day, we departed around 20 minutes late because a few children arrived late. The driver warned us this might impact the return pickup time as he had another job to do in between. Fair enough. We accepted responsibility for the delay and expected perhaps a 20-minute knock-on effect later in the day.

For the avoidance of doubt - because I fully expect this company to dispute it - we did not leave “30 minutes late” as the manager later aggressively claimed. I know for a fact it was 20 minutes because I have a WhatsApp message timestamped 13:22 to the delayed child’s mother saying: “Don’t worry, we’ve got him now and are on our way.” So if we are splitting hairs, let’s at least stick to reality.

What followed was absolute chaos.

When our scheduled pickup time (17:00) came and went with no update, I called the driver expecting a short delay. Instead, he smugly informed me he was “40 minutes away because you made us leave late.” He eventually arrived 50 minutes after the agreed pickup time (17:50), leaving me stranded with 15 overstimulated 10-year-old boys while anxious parents repeatedly called asking where we were.

Then, around 20 minutes into the return journey, the driver abruptly pulled into an M25 service station and announced he needed to take a mandatory 45-minute break because he had “gone over hours.” The children were left effectively killing time in a petrol station while he took his break. Once again, the blame was placed entirely on our original 20-minute delay. He would not even engage in any form of conversation with myself or my husband, and as soon as we started questioning anything he threatened to discontinue the journey.

At this point, during the middle of this entire fiasco, the MANAGER phoned me directly. I genuinely wish I had recorded the conversation because it was one of the most bizarre and unprofessional customer service calls I have ever experienced.

Not only did he repeatedly call me “honey” despite me asking several times to stop and use my actual name, but he immediately launched into aggressive accusations instead of beginning with even the most basic apology for the situation.

He accused me of somehow “coercing” the driver into continuing the journey - while I was simultaneously supervising 15 children and fielding calls from worried parents. The accusation was absurd.

Even more bizarrely, he then warned me “not to become racist.” I have never seen this guy and have no idea what he looks like, and I am literally a person of colour myself. When I asked him what on earth he was talking about, his response was simply: “Just saying.”

Throughout the call, both the driver and manager kept insisting that every single issue stemmed from our 20-minute delayed departure. When I pointed out that this made absolutely no mathematical sense - because a 20-minute delay does not somehow justify a 50-minute late pickup and a driver running out of legal driving hours - the manager then suddenly changed tack and admitted, “Oh yes, there was traffic too.”

So the explanation constantly changed, but one thing remained consistent: not a single genuine apology or shred of accountability from anyone involved.

I have genuinely never experienced such impudent, defensive, chaotic, and deeply unprofessional service in my life. No ownership, no safeguarding awareness, no respect for customers, and absolutely appalling communication throughout.

Avoid this company at all costs.

We were also in the market for more machinery, but after this experience we will be taking our business elsewhere. I would strongly advise anyone considering dealing with this company to avoid them entirely. Their communication is shocking, their word clearly means nothing, and they have no issue going back on agreements without even informing the customer.

I write this review in both of my position as a patient and as medical doctor myself. My wife and I had 4 rounds of treatment at nurture fertility through the access fertility programme.  We previously had 2 rounds of treatment in Sheffield prior to this, so have experienced both NHS care and private care.

I always had the sentiment that when opting for private care I would expect to actually have more of a say in the care compared to the NHS and that the care would be more personalised. However our collective experience was the opposite.

We consistently found that there was poor communication across the team. We literally felt like a number rather than a patient. Every appointment felt short and rushed except during the egg collection.

There was limited communication with the doctors. The treatment plan was varied between each cycle which was a positive aspect, other than the 2nd round of treatment, none of them mentioned any holistic aspects that we should consider to improve our chances.

I did enquire at one point regarding the use of HCG and was categorically told this was a bad idea. However when seeking medical care elsewhere this was prescribed and subsequently improved my parameters.

Luckily I am in the position where I can afford to pay more treatment cycles however I would really sympathise with patients who might ever only be able to afford a single cycle. I don't really feel the care is personalised and I would recommend using another clinic.

I instructed KBS Corporate to sell my business after seeing a mixed range of reviews. They charge a significant upfront fee, which covers the creation of marketing materials.

Unfortunately, my experience was disappointing - particularly due to the lack of transparency and communication.

Despite repeatedly requesting it, I was not provided with basic information such as:

- The names of companies approached on my behalf
- Dates of contact
- Any feedback received

After several months, I was given a single spreadsheet. A year later, I made multiple further requests for an updated list, but nothing was ever provided. This led me to question whether their focus is primarily on onboarding clients for upfront fees, or prioritising larger deals where commission is higher.

I have since cut ties with KBS. From the point of signing, I never felt like a priority. A broker’s core responsibilities should include:

1.	Approaching suitable prospective buyers
2.	Gathering feedback
3.	Sharing that feedback with their client

On one occasion, I was also concerned by how pushy KBS were in arranging a meeting with a prospective buyer. The individual provided only a screenshot of a spreadsheet as proof of identity - something I later found online myself. Despite this, KBS still encouraged the meeting. We ultimately withdrew, as it was clearly a bogus or scam situation.

I raised concerns about the lack of transparency and may have benefited from a different representative to represent our company but this never happened. One that could actually be bothered.

To be clear, this review is not about failing to sell the business. We did receive one offer - but that came from a contact we introduced ourselves, who had already shown prior interest.

This review is about the lack of communication, transparency, and overall engagement throughout the process.

But within thirty minutes, life shifted - so I cancelled. Calmly, reasonably, with 3.5 hours still stretching ahead like open road. In any honest kitchen, nothing would have even begun. No flames lit. No pans touched. No effort wasted.

Except, according to Hong Kong House, everything already had.

They claimed my food was in preparation. Already cooking. Already committed. As if time itself had bent for them - as if they had rushed to prepare a meal hours before it was ever needed. And if that were true (if they truly had made it then) what was I meant to receive? A cold, stale shadow of a meal? Something left to sit, to sweat, to decay in a box for hours before reaching me?

It doesn’t make sense. It never did.

Because this wasn’t truth.

It was an excuse.

And with that excuse, they took my money and closed the door.

When I called, I wasn’t angry -not yet. I was expecting, at the very least, a conversation. Some shred of decency. A moment of understanding.

Instead, I was met with something sharp, immediate, and unapologetic.

Hostility.

No explanation. No accountability. Just a voice that cut over mine, dismissing, belittling - and then, plainly, calling me “stupid.” As if questioning something so obviously wrong made me the problem. As if I should accept being taken advantage of in silence.

And that’s the moment everything changed.

It stopped being about food.

It stopped being about money.

It became about being disrespected, outright and without hesitation, by a business that didn’t just fail - but chose to.

A choice to lie.

A choice to keep what wasn’t theirs.

A choice to treat a customer not as a person, but as something disposable.

There was no food.

No refund.

No apology.

Just the hollow, infuriating reality of being dismissed and spoken down to - as though fairness was too much to ask.

Some takeaways leave you disappointed.

Hong Kong House leaves you angry - and worse, unheard.

This isn’t about “rules” anymore. This is about lack of understanding, lack of fairness, and zero care for the community.
People in Middleton need to start speaking up. Why is everyone quiet about this? Why aren’t more people raising this on Facebook, tagging the centre, and demanding change?

Update :

purchased a vehicle from GS Motor Group on 22/02/2026. From day 2, the vehicle has suffered ongoing faults and, as of 13/04/2026, it remains off the road and unusable. This is completely unacceptable for a vehicle sold as fit for purpose, particularly as it was required as a family vehicle.

Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, goods supplied must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose, and as described. Based on my experience, this vehicle has failed to meet those standards from the outset.

While the dealership has now covered certain repair costs (including a water pump and seals), this does not resolve the underlying issue  the vehicle has been unreliable since purchase and has caused significant disruption, financial loss, and stress due to being without transport.

The Dealership now does not want to communicate with the finance company and it shows a lack of acknowledgment from thier end showing that it was the wrong company to do business with, all they really cared for was thier pockets, and putting a a customer out of pocket.

I also have serious concerns regarding the so-called “3-month warranty.” In practice, this has not provided meaningful support. Instead, I have experienced delays, lack of clarity, and ultimately being told that key issues are not covered. A warranty should not be used to deflect responsibility where faults were present or developing at the point of sale.

Furthermore, I was fully transparent when part-exchanging my previous vehicle, including clearly disclosing that it was a categorised vehicle and providing the logbook. It is therefore concerning that this has since been disputed telling the finance company he didn’t know it was a category vehicle is absurd and shocking.

Overall, this situation raises concerns around:
•	The condition of the vehicle at the point of sale
•	Whether faults were adequately disclosed
•	The adequacy and honesty of aftersales support
•	The handling of a legitimate consumer dispute

I am currently pursuing this matter formally with the finance company and legal representation, and I am prepared to escalate further if required.

I would strongly advise others to exercise caution and ensure full independent checks are carried out before purchasing.

Hero Man & Van made the usual stress of moving day a complete nightmare due to their numerous failings and have refused to take any accountability, to the point where I had to raise a dispute with my bank to get some of my money back.

The ‘package’ I paid for was £545 for 2 men and 1 Luton box van, for 4 hours. I was explicitly clear in all my correspondence that I needed help with bulky items only, as I had plenty of helpers/vehicles on hand to move boxes and smaller items. I had also moved the year prior, so I knew that 1 van would be sufficient.

On the day, I was informed there was an hour delay, which I was able to accommodate. In hindsight, this seemed to give them the green light to mess me about, because after that initial call, no one contacted me again and I had to keep calling to find out what on earth was going on. Each time, I was told they were an hour away, and each time, no one turned up.
I was moving out of a rental property which had a tenant moving into it that day, so having to repeatedly call an increasingly disgruntled landlord about MORE delays was immensely stressful.

Almost 3 HOURS later, 3 men, with 2 vans turned up.
The second van (I was not told about and did not consent to) caused disruption to the narrow cul-de-sac, meaning neighbours had to move off their drives to accommodate it.

Two of the men were pleasant and got on with the job, but the third man, who I believe was a temp, thought it was appropriate to stand and brag about how much money he was making that day and make sexist comments about my ability to pack up an entire house by myself - ‘you must be strong, it’s nice to see a woman doing something useful for a change’.
Unsurprisingly, he was later seen being heavy-handed with my belongings.

The men traipsed mud throughout the ground floor of the rental (despite there being back garden access) moments before the landlord was due to arrive, which put my deposit in jeopardy.

Within 24hrs I reported a broken tv plug and addressed that the job had been completed in less than the 4 hours I had paid for. I was instantly dismissed, despite being told when I booked that ‘if it can be done quicker, we’ll look after you’ i.e. refund you the extra (see email screenshot).

The job was completed in 2 hours, and I was being charged for 4. I was charged £545 for 2 hours.

For weeks the company invalidated me, before my bank stepped in and got me the partial refund I was due.

I realised after unpacking that I also had dents in white goods, smashed crockery and missing garden items. My washing machine, which was new, now makes an unsettling rattling noise.

I’d recommend not signing anything until you’ve fully unpacked and checked over your belongings - they tried using this against me in my dispute (and again in their response below!) stating that because I signed, I was ‘happy with the service’. Unbelievable! It seems to be their way of capitalising from the stress/chaos of moving day.

How a company handles complaints around its failings reveals its values and priorities and is a true representation of its character. The issues I raised throughout this ordeal were either met with dismissal or ignored entirely.

The manner in which he has spoken to them has always come across as arrogant and  rude. He appears very judgemental and opinionated  and my youngest daughter who was around 4 at the time has been left in tears. However we did keep going and never complained.
I have witnessed on several visits him talking down to dental nurses and being very sharp with them.
On several visits he has contradicted himself and told me my daughters have had treatment that I know they haven't had.   This has lead me to have absolutely no confidence in his ability as a dentist.
Recently I posted a one star review on here after recieving the usual experience. My oldest daughter was midway through treatment to have teeth removed to make room for braces. I made an appointment for this and confirmed it the week before, when we arrived we were told it was only for them to look in her mouth, when I explained that we were led to believe it was for an extraction I was spoken down to and basically told I was lying and  that the  receptionist would have never said this to me. After putting the one star review I spoke to the practice about an appointment and was questioned by the dental nurse as to why I had done this as Nima Namin had read it and wasn't happy with this. I was told he stated  that he felt uncomfortable seeing my daughters again. I just couldn't believe that half way through treatment he was potentially going to stop seeing her and that he was the one who felt uncomfortable after years of it being us.
The receptionist later contacted me and said that Nima had said he felt he could no longer treat both my daughters as communication had broken down. I just couldn't believe this after putting a one star review my daughter's were taken off his books and left without a dentist part way through treatment.
When I look  back he has actually done us  a favour. We have since found a lovely dental practice where my children feel happy to attend not anxious and worried like before. They are greeted and spoken to like human beings. After speaking to others who attend Smile Care centre they say they have had exactly the same experience as us.
My own elderly  mother used to attend and had her remaining teeth removed by Namin without being told. She was told it was for a check up, as she had been told previously she would have to go to the hospital to have this done  as she was a high risk patient with heart failure and other chronic health conditions, along with having a phobia of the dentist.  When she left she was shaking and so upset, she never went back.
I just deeply regret not leaving sooner, and if anyone is thinking of joining this dentist please don't .

I  am extremely disappointed with the lack of communication and support from David Lloyds Derby. I submitted a refund request in March 2026 and have sent numerous follow-up emails since then, yet I have received no acknowledgment or response.

As a loyal member, I expected a much higher level of service, especially regarding such an important issue. This ongoing silence has left me feeling undervalued and frustrated.

Today was a very sad day seeing the condition of the tennis courts. It was a beautiful, sunny day — perfect weather to go and play tennis. After getting up early and heading out before work so we could enjoy an afternoon of tennis, we arrived at the bubble only to find the courts covered in leaves. The net on the main court was lying on the ground, there were no benches because they had been left outside the bubble on the grass, and everything was dirty in general.

It’s very disappointing considering the amount of money we pay and the lack of maintenance carried out on the facilities for members to enjoy them. In their current condition, much of the club’s facilities simply do not reflect the monthly fees we pay, and it’s honestly impossible to recommend this club to any friends.

I absolutely love this place, which makes writing this even more disappointing. I’m sharing this not just from my own experience, but on behalf of many members who are having to leave due to the continual price increases, which are becoming unaffordable for a lot of people. It’s genuinely starting to impact the amazing community that made this place so special.

It feels as though the focus is on selling the dream initially, but once you’re a long-standing member, support becomes difficult to access. Enquiries are often directed to an AI assistant on the app or a slow email response, and it’s frustrating that there’s no one on-site available to speak with directly about membership concerns.

There also needs to be more transparency around access to other locations under the same tiered membership. While it’s advertised that you can use multiple locations across the country, there are strict limitations that aren’t always made clear upfront. Some members have found themselves moved into higher tiers having visited other locations, with direct debits increasing significantly, up to £300 per month in some cases and requesting this to be amended being near impossible with an AI assistant.

It’s really upsetting, and it doesn’t make customers feel valued or supported. I’ve also seen many people feel misled by how appealing the memberships are presented, particularly for those of us who work hybrid or travel around the country, where flexibility is a key selling point.

It was even more disappointing to see the Derby tier reduced without clear notice, reportedly due to a drop in food hygiene rating, with members effectively being penalised as a result of something outside of their control.

I’m saddened to leave this review, but it reflects a consistent experience. Many members are leaving feeling unsupported and undervalued, which is a real shame given how great this place could continue to be.

I’m extremely disappointed with my experience. I underwent rhinoplasty to correct a noticeably crooked nose and a visible lump. While the surgeon did slightly reduce the lump from the profile view, the overall result is far from what was promised. One side of my nose was essentially left untouched, and it remains visibly uneven and crooked. I questioned whether he forgot about that side and even he seemed visibly surprised at the state of it.

The changes made were minimal to the point of being barely noticeable, especially considering the significant cost of the procedure. I expected a meaningful improvement, but instead I feel like very little was actually done.

What is even more frustrating is the lack of accountability during the follow-up. I was told that this was “the best that could be done,” which felt dismissive and did not reflect the concerns I raised. There was no willingness to acknowledge the unsatisfactory outcome vs what he had deemed a completely reasonable and achievable goal pre-op and he did not discuss potential solutions, not that I would trust him with any more money for a second operation.

I completely understand that, in many cases, achieving the desired outcome from rhinoplasty may require more than one procedure. However, I feel misled by the clear gap between what was promised and the actual result. one_star_reviews.text:
I took my wedding dress to be dry cleaned here after our abroad wedding, ready to be worn again for our UK reception.

Upon collecting my dress I was not informed of any issues during the cleaning process and was assured that everything had gone well.

However when I was trying my dress on the week before the reception, I noticed that the thread holding the pleats in place had come loose and a section of buttons were missing from the back of the dress.

Absolutely horrified by this realisation at such a close proximity to my reception I quickly made arrangements for the repairs to take place. I emailed Paul at Pennywise and he offered a very sincere apology and refunded the cleaning services. I was then told that he would investigate how this happened and that their wedding dress specialist would be in touch. I cannot fault Paul at all for his customer service.

However, when I received the call from the wedding dress specialist, I was met with nothing but excuses with the intention of trying to absolve themselves from blame. It was implied that I was merely being dramatic about my dress being ruined as it "only needed some buttons reattaching and a tac stitch putting back in".

The fact that my dress was not "completely ruined" was besides the point. The point was that my wedding dress (that I was due to wear again in less than a week) was not returned to me in a wearable condition. Had I have not checked in advance, I would not have been able to wear this dress as it was to my reception. The point is also that my wedding dress cost well over £1000 (which also made it more expensive to get cleaned in the first instance) therefore any damage at all is in fact a big deal.

It's also worth mentioning that I had no reason to check the dress in advance as at no point was it ever mentioned to us that there had been any issues during the cleaning process. I was very lucky that I had the forethought to check the dress in advance. What this evidently tells me is that either the dress was not checked prior to returning to me, or they were in fact trying to decieve a customer by not informing me of the damage that had occurred.

Had she just held her hands up and admitted that some mistake was made here, I would have been satisfied with the outcome of this ordeal.

I therefore advise that if you value honesty and candour in your services, I would get your wedding dress cleaned elsewhere.

Chronicles of the Yellow Containers – The Spear of Truth

The sun sank weary and pale over the smoky horizon of Brunton-Nether, like the final, guttering breath of a dying dragon. Baron S. Cardos stood in the yard of the great manufactory, his cloak torn and buffeted by the icy wind. In this realm, honor had long since been bartered away to the cold gods of steel and machine grease.

Before his feet lay the Yellow Dolavs. They were massive, dark, and looming—resembling the abandoned nests of the Dark Dragon Queen herself. They were filled with the rot of negligence, and their contents seeped out to poison the very earth.

“My Lords,” Cardos spoke, his voice ringing like cold steel upon stone within the crumbling walls of Solamnia. “The containers are filled to the brim. The order is broken. If we do not act, this darkness shall devour every soul within these walls!”

But the Council of Management only offered a mocking smile. The high chieftain of the realm, Lord Vowe Dotes, watched the events from his high tower. He was the "King," whose word was law, yet who preferred the shifting shadows to the clarity of open speech.

The Song of the Chronicles on the Great Betrayal:

The Fading of the Spring Sunlight (April 2023): The first warning cry was raised, like a distant horn blast before the coming of a storm. But the answer was not aid; it was a Deathly Silence.

The Treachery of the Summer Heat (July 2023): At last, Lord Vowe Dotes himself deigned to speak. The High Chieftain tossed a few words to the restless seeker, like a bone to a stray dog. “I have spoken to the sub-chiefs,” he etched upon the parchment, but his words were as hollow as a plundered dwarven mine.

The yellow monsters remained in the mud, bloated with the venom of irresponsibility, mocking all that was once called safety. But the Wheel of Fate turned inexorably. It was not danger, but Betrayal that finally overtook Baron S. Cardos. It was then that an ancient power awoke—a force mortals call Whistleblowing.

The cult of the Yellow Crate now performs dark rituals, trying to rewrite the past with forged runes on altered scrolls. But Baron S. Cardos knows: the truth is like Dragon-glass. Cold, sharp, and capable of slicing through even Lord Vowe Dotes’ thickest armor of lies.

The Moral:
Safety may be a discarded weapon in the hands of the weak. But the Truth is like the Dragonlance: once it finds its mark, no High Chieftain can halt the fall.

I very rarely leave reviews like this, but this needs to be said.

I signed up for this event in mid-2025 and fully disclosed my medical history, including a brain injury from 8 years ago. This was accepted through their own process without issue.

The original event was scheduled for December 12th, but was then postponed due to “unforeseen circumstances.” Fair enough — these things happen. However, from that point onward, the organisation was poor and only got worse.

The registration/Q&A meeting at Sandy Park was a clear example of this. There was no signage, no direction, no clear communication — and for anyone who knows Sandy Park, it’s a large venue. People were left wandering around trying to figure out where to go. It was disorganised, unclear, and poorly managed from the outset.

Despite that, I carried on. I committed months of training, fundraising, and promotion. I pushed ticket sales heavily, including selling a full table and additional standing tickets. I was actively backing this event and putting my name behind it.

Then, two days before the training camp, I was told I could no longer participate — due to the exact same medical history that had already been disclosed and accepted months earlier.

That is not just frustrating — it’s a complete failure in basic organisation and process. This should have been addressed at the very beginning, not after months of commitment, promotion, and financial involvement.
What makes this even worse is the complete lack of communication since. People who purchased tickets through me — some spending over £300 — have been chasing refunds. They’ve been ignored. I am extremely disappointed with the concierge and management team at Novella, and I want to share my experience as a reference for anyone considering moving here.

When I first purchased my flat, I already had a very negative experience with a female member of staff whose attitude was rude, dismissive and not welcoming. From what I understand, many other residents have had similar experiences with her.

More recently, my key was accidentally dropped into the elevator well in March. I reported this to the concierge and was told that it would be collected in April when the engineer came. However, no one contacted me afterwards, and I was never given any update.

Since then, I have followed up around six or seven times in person with multiple members of staff. Each time, I was either told that someone would get back to me or that the information would be passed on, but I never received any clear response. It genuinely felt as if my request was simply being ignored.

I then went to the concierge desk again, where a member of staff took my contact details and the relevant information. I was told I would receive a response, but almost a week passed and I still heard nothing. Eventually, after countless attempts and emails, I finally received a very brief two-sentence reply saying they were still contacting the engineer — which is exactly the same answer I was given nearly two months ago.

As residents and owners, we pay a yearly service charge, and I believe basic communication and timely responses should be part of the service we receive. Instead, I have been ignored repeatedly and treated rudely. It is very disappointing that the service charge continues to increase each year while the quality of management and communication remains so poor.

As an owner at Novella, I would strongly suggest that anyone considering moving here thinks carefully before making a decision. The building itself may be a nice place to live, but the management team and concierge service can significantly reduce your quality of living.

had an extremely disappointing experience with Katie Sanderson at Holden Smith.

What should have been a relatively straightforward property sale turned into an 18-month ordeal. As a direct result of repeated delays, unnecessary requests, and poor communication, I estimate that this experience cost me approximately £45,000.

This financial loss included:

A forced reduction of the sale price by £20,000
Ongoing mortgage payments
Council tax
Service charges and other holding costs
Additional management pack fees and related expenses

During the first sale, an insurance claim that was unrelated to my property was raised as an issue. Even after the insurance company confirmed that they could not provide the information being requested, there appeared to be no practical workaround. The transaction stalled and the first buyer withdrew.

When a second buyer was found, all documentation was already in place, including the management pack. Despite confirmation from the managing agent that nothing had changed, I was asked to purchase a new management pack at additional cost, causing further delay.

Communication was extremely frustrating. Emails often went unanswered for days, and on several occasions I was told that documents were outstanding when they had already been supplied.

The cumulative impact of these delays was severe. I was left carrying the property for many additional months and ultimately accepted a significantly lower sale price.

In my opinion, the process demonstrated poor communication, a lack of urgency, and little appreciation for the financial consequences to the client.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend Katie Sanderson or Holden Smith.

When we arrived, the experience was completely different. As soon as I mentioned my allergy to the man serving us, he immediately said that everything was cooked in nut oil. BillyOh and Garden Buildings Direct don’t just sell garden buildings — they sell frustration, wasted weekends, and unresolved problems. If you are considering buying from them, don’t. This has been an astonishingly bad experience, and one I would never willingly repeat.

I am extremely disappointed with both the product quality and customer service provided by this company.

We purchased a new Wendy house supplied in multiple parts. While each bag included a parts list, the contents were completely mixed, requiring us to open every bag and manually measure components to identify them. This made the initial stages unnecessarily time-consuming.

The quality of the wood was highly inconsistent. Some pieces appeared new and well-finished, while others looked as though they had been stored in damp conditions for an extended period. In addition, several components did not match the dimensions stated in the instructions. Some key structural beams were warped or incorrectly cut, resulting in an uneven overall construction.

No printed instructions were provided—only an online manual. This made assembly more difficult, as I had to repeatedly scroll through the document on my phone to locate part dimensions for each step.

The most significant issue arose during roof assembly. The instructions specify roof boards at 143mm in width; however, all supplied boards were approximately 20mm shorter. This prevented the required overhang from being formed, making the next stage of construction impossible.

Additionally, the supplied screws were insufficient to complete even half of the build, forcing me to purchase additional materials at my own expense.

I contacted customer service to resolve these issues. The process itself was frustrating—image uploads were limited to 10MB per file, and despite being advised I could upload multiple images in one ticket, the system only allowed one per submission. I was then instructed to create multiple tickets, which was both inefficient and time-consuming.

After reviewing my evidence, the company acknowledged some parts were substandard but claimed this would not affect structural integrity. They agreed to send replacement roof boards and additional screws. However, the replacements were also incorrect (still undersized), and the quantity of screws provided was insufficient.

When I raised this again, I received inconsistent and contradictory responses. At one point, I was told that smaller boards may be sent if correct ones are out of stock, and that I should simply use more of them to compensate. This does not align with the design specifications and does not resolve the issue of the missing overhang.

At this stage, I requested a full refund and return. I was informed that I would need to cover the return shipping costs, despite the product being faulty and incomplete.

In summary, I received a product that was of poor quality, incorrectly specified, and incomplete. The customer service experience only added to the frustration, with unclear guidance and inadequate resolutions offered.

I would strongly advise others to consider alternative suppliers.

I attended their Ready, Set, Bloom event here and as stall holders, this was one of the worst event experiences we’ve had.

The event was severely lacking in organisation and promotion. Footfall was practically non-existent—only friends and family of other stall holders attended. There was no clear signage for the event, and even finding the farm itself was difficult, which only made the situation worse.

In the lead-up, communication from Lexy raised concerns, with repeated mentions of financial struggles and requests for further support. Stall holders were also encouraged to “invest” in Honey Nook C.I.C with promises of shelf space in a farm shop and access to exclusive events. However, there was no visible shop on site, and this has not been delivered as expected.

Following the event, several stall holders requested refunds for the £15 shop investment. These requests appeared to be ignored, and shortly afterwards Lexy left the group chat. To date, no refunds have been received.

On the day itself, there was no effort to meet, greet, or support stall holders. While poor turnout can happen, the complete lack of acknowledgement or apology from the organisers, including Bridget, was incredibly disappointing. Instead, stall holders were told to pack up early at 2pm, despite the event being advertised until 4pm.

Basic facilities were also not adequate, with no proper access to toilets, running water, or handwashing facilities.

Overall, a very frustrating and disheartening experience that left many people out of pocket. Based on this experience, we would strongly recommend others think carefully before committing to events or any financial involvement here.

Be very cautious when buying from Arctic Cabins (AC), after doing my research I decided to go with AC even though it was much more expensive than their competitors. My reasoning was down to warranty, AC offered a 10 year warranty on most of the cabin if it was assembled by their approved contractors, due to the price of these structures I felt the extra money would be worth it.

On contacting AC they provided details of their Scottish distributors who were Scotia Cabins, I bought a 10m cabin which was installed November 2022.

In 2025 AC stopped using Scotia as their Scottish distributor, leaving a void north of the border.

Just over 3 years from having the cabin installed I discovered the plywood pelmets which form the lower part of the roof were rotting with major water ingress (picture attached). This appears to be a common issue with these cabins with various discussion on the subject on a number of Facebook pages.

On contacting Scotia I was advised this was a manufacturer issue and advised to contact AC for assistance. AC customer service was worse than useless, obviously they no longer have agents covering Scotland and are not prepared to honour their guarantee that they claim come with an approved installation.  Eventually after involving Trading Standards they have agreed to provide the parts but won’t fund the labour costs, although we will have to wait and see if the parts actually arrive.

Very poor service from a company that apparently prides itself on the quality of its cabins, my advice would be look at the cheaper options, they are just good! Also any negative comments on their owners facebook group which they admin will get you banned (they don’t appreciate honest feedback).

I have given them 2 stars rather than 1 as apart from the poor quality of materials they use for the roof, the rest of the structure seems fine (after 3 years anyway).

In reply to Arctic Cabins response:

Thanks AC for taking the time to reply to my honest and frank review, shame you couldn't do so on your Facebook owners club page, but I guess there you can control unfavourable reviews by banning members. A couple of points which I believe you are not in dispute of

1. On contacting yourselves when I was in the market to purchase a cabin, you provided me the details of Scotia Cabins who you told me were your representatives for Scotland.

2. You supplied Scotia Cabins with the cabin, thus you are there manufacturer.

3. I never said Trading Standards had contacted yourself, I contacted them for advice, gave them the full circumstances and they advised me that the installer (Scotia Cabins) are responsible for the first 6 months after installation, then the manufacturer (yourselves) are responsible for any further guarantee period after the 6 months. The chap said it was like purchasing a Samsung phone from Amazon, Samsung are responsible for warranty repairs. I did mention this to Rob when I spoke to him, it was at that point he offered to provide the materials including shipping to Scotia Cabins.

I planned on reviewing this rating depending on how things went with the manufacturer warranty for the poor workmanship which has caused water damage. Initially Arctic Cabins agreed to replace the damaged part after many communications through their distributor Scotia Cabins. Alas they have not lived up to their promises and have failed to supply the part. It is now mid April, this has been going on since January. Rather than have the damage spread, I have paid in full to arrange for a repair, so if you are thinking of a BBQ hut, don’t expect Arctic Cabins to honour their manufacturer guarantee. For this reason I have reduced my initial rating by a further star

On 1st May 2026, I was finally told that the chain had collapsed entirely and the property was no longer in a position to be sold.

As a direct result of relying on the information provided, I have incurred significant financial costs and have now been left without accommodation and effectively homeless.

This situation suggests that Richard Watkinson either failed to properly establish the chain status at the outset or communicated inaccurate information throughout the process. I would strongly advise others to steer well clear of these agents as they are clearly incapable of providing a service which should be standard by an established estate agent

I applied to the University of Hull for the September 2025 intake with high hopes for my future. Unfortunately, my UK student visa was refused on 6 October 2025 after the interview. Following this, I immediately contacted the university to request a refund of my tuition fees.

I sent multiple emails but did not receive any response for a long time. On 17 October, I sent my first formal refund request. However, the university only responded after 3–4 months, which was extremely frustrating and stressful.

In their reply, they stated that their refund policy had been updated on 6 November and claimed that I was not eligible for a refund because I had not applied for an administrative review. This was unfair because my visa refusal was based on an interview, and I was not properly guided about this requirement at the time.

Despite this, I followed their instructions and submitted an appeal. Unfortunately, the university responded again with the same decision, refusing my refund.

This experience has been very disappointing. As an international student, this was my hard-earned money, and losing it like this is extremely difficult. I expected better support, clearer guidance, and more timely communication from the university.

I sincerely hope the university improves its support system for international students and handles such cases with more fairness and understanding.

On arrival, you're informed that there actually are quite a few limits on how this works. You're allowed to order 8 dishes every 15 minutes, only 8 of these can be the more expensive Sashimi style dishes, which I suppose is fair enough, and you can pay extra for "exclusive" dishes. Drinks are not included, also understandable. The food was nice enough, although almost always much smaller than, less portions and not including some of the components shown on the menu pictures. The cocktails were nice but again very small for the cost and not really 'gourmet' enough to justify dinkiness. The atmosphere was probably nice when it first opened but the decor is looking a little tired. Then came the bill. When we requested the bill and attendant came over to inform us that there was a hidden charge for every left over dish. We were at no point informed about this prior to the meal, and were obviously pretty annoyed when the bill was already over £100 for two people. I obviously understand and support a food waste charge but it needs to be made really clear to diners prior to ordering because it would have completely changed the way we ordered. We only had a couple of Bao Buns, some Japanese pickles and some meat skewers left which we took home to eat for lunch the next day, anything else which was left over was because it didn't taste very nice. After a 'discussion' with the manager they did reasonably agreed to only add a £3 charge to our bill rather than £3 per dish, however having to argue with staff was an unpleasant end to our date night and left a nasty taste. We visited Tsuki Japanese Restaurant within the last week and, sadly, we won’t be returning.

The concept has potential, but right now the experience feels hard work rather than enjoyable.

When we arrived, the restaurant was around half empty and lacked any real atmosphere. As a group of six (five adults and one child), we headed to the bar for a drink, but were asked by a waitress to return to the entrance foyer to be seated properly. This felt odd given how quiet the restaurant was.

We were also told the extractor system in the kitchen was broken, which meant the front door had to be propped open. Unfortunately, we were seated right next to it and spent the entire meal freezing, to the point where we kept our coats on. We raised this a few times, but the only solution offered was a small fan, which made little difference, it genuinely felt like sitting outside.

We opted for the buffet at £39 per head (rising to £45 at weekends, which felt unusual), and were given an iPad to order all food and drinks. The system was clunky and confusing, especially for some of our group. One person hadn’t brought their glasses, and another was 70, so passing one device around made it slow and frustrating, taking several minutes per person just to place an order.

It would have been far better for a member of staff to take the first round of orders and bring something simple like miso soup while we got settled. Instead, we were left trying to navigate the system in a cold restaurant, which took away from the whole experience.

Food took around 45 minutes to arrive and, when it did, it was just OK, not bad, but certainly not worth the price given everything else , also no child option on the food, and you had to pay extra for deserts!

Overall, it’s a shame, because with a few improvements, particularly around service, ordering, and basic comfort, it could be a really good place. But as it stands, the experience just isn’t there, and unfortunately we wouldn’t return or recommend it.
£100+

Seven of us went to the Fox and Goose to celebrate my mum’s birthday, and it turned out to be the worst meal any of us have ever had.

After ordering, we waited an hour and ten minutes before any food arrived. When my steak finally came, I’d asked for it rare—but it was cooked well done. I sent it back, only for the replacement to come out medium-well, which still wasn’t what I ordered.My daughter ordered the burger which was that dry It snapped in half.

My mum’s salmon was even worse—it arrived raw. She sent it back twice, and even after that, 25 minutes later, it still hadn’t come back out—despite everyone else having finished their meals. At that point, she’d had enough and just wanted to leave.

Completely unacceptable service, terrible food, and a ruined birthday celebration. None of us will ever be back.

ORIGINAL POST:
Back in April 2025 while searching for new tariffs and energy providers, I had completed an accidental sign up on huddle. The following day I cancelled of which they accepted closure on those terms and within a 14 day cooling of period.

This goes on for 10 MONTHS as I formally dispute there claims of which they were aggressive with there billings and notices. They even sent a welfare check which essentially is a home visit by someone wearing a body cam, a bit embarrassing when you have guests over. They additionally blocked 5 switch requests during this period, of which they only notified myself in December they were blocking switches. I did my research and challenged that this was an erroneous transfer, the response was that it was a ‘deemed contract’. They pushed so hard on the position that it was a deemed contract to a point I started believing them and was pushed into a position where I was accepting I had to pay under a deemed contract, at this point it’s £380 under deemed contract rates but would still have had to provide meter reading s for more accurate billing to be charged.

While at the same time I was investigating Homebox Ltd for incorrect billing as the ad been charging myself for gas supply when there was no gas supply being paid as Huddle and Tru Energy had hi jacked the gas supply. I was claiming over charges from Homebox Ltd to settle the payments to huddle when my guy said I’m still right, I then bypassed huddle and went straight to Tru energy, requested an erroneous transfer request, explained what happened and they responded that I don’t qualify for a erroneous transfer request, responded back straight away and put every thing in point form:

-accidental sign up
-I cancelled they accepted
-no contract exists.
-14 day cooling off period.
-huddle switch team put request in on 10 April after I cancelled.
-you took over supply on the 30 April 2025.

Then tru energy came back and said yes that is erroneous transfer and and will raise it on my behalf.

10 MONTHS stuck between Huddle and Homebox Ltd of the worst bundle energy companies around, 10 months of complete stress to educate them on misrepresentation, false claims, unlawful gain practices and basic understanding of Ofgem rules.

Homebox Ltd recently closed my acc after law enforcement complaints and has review the over charges and compensating £450 for over charges on the gas supply.

Huddle has offers £120 for the inconvienece!

Huddle I would expect as a maximum the basic erroneous transfer error compensation under the ofgem guidelines and at most the average usage you so clearly stated in your most recent bill to the value of £700 as compensation for the length, stress and the out of my own pocket problem YOUR mistake has caused.

I am going to be required to cover a bill to Octopus Energy now for a gas supply for the past 10 months.

You need to act responsibly and accountable in your conduct and the damage it has caused.

STAY AWAY FROM HUDDLE!!! NOTHING BUT HELL, I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND TO MY WORST ENEMY

An account was created in my name and I was switched from my previous energy supplier onto a far more expensive tariff without my knowledge or consent. To this day, I still do not understand how this happened. When I realised what had happened, I contacted Huddle by phone and email to cancel and dispute the account, only to be told it was “too late” and that I would face cancellation fees despite never agreeing to the switch in the first place.

From there, the entire situation became a nightmare. I received constant automated emails, texts, and payment demands for charges I was disputing. Responses to my emails appeared to go unanswered, whilst automated bot email payment reminders continued almost daily for bills that were significantly more than my previous supplier.

I later discovered Huddle had sent enforcement officers to my rental property, charging me £60 per visit simply to post letters through a letterbox at a property I do not live at.

Things escalated even further when the property was switched onto a prepayment meter without my consent. The house is fully electric with no gas supply, and this left 7 tenants without electricity, heating, hot water, Wi-Fi, cooking facilities, and security systems. An emergency electrician had to be called out before discovering the issue was the meter we were unaware of had run out of credit.

At the time I was backpacking abroad with very limited connectivity, and despite my managing agent explaining the seriousness of the situation affecting multiple tenants, Huddle refused to speak with him because the disputed account was created in my name. In the end, the only way he could get the electricity restored was by pretending to be me on the phone!

To finally leave Huddle, I was told I had to clear all alleged debt on the account, including enforcement charges and cancellation fees. I reluctantly paid £1,094 just to escape the situation and in order to switch back to my previous supplier. I was also told that the £200 credit I had recently topped up onto the meter would be refunded, which never happened.

Months later, despite no longer being with Huddle, they charged me £364 from my bank account unexpectedly. I never knowingly authorised this payment and can only assume my card details had been stored from a previous over the phone meter top-up. I then found more automated bot erroneous emails in my spam folder claiming I had an outstanding £0 balance on my account, to which monthly scheduled payments of £364 will be made to recover the outstanding debt of £0 – made no sense!

Trying to contact customer service has been one of the most frustrating parts of this entire ordeal. Calls are placed on hold endlessly, staff are unable to explain anything properly, callbacks never happen, and I have even been hung up on multiple times. I ended up having to cancel my bank card to avoid these unauthorised Huddle charges from continuing.

Now, despite previously settling the account and it being half a year since leaving Huddle for another energy provider, I am once again receiving threatening legal emails about alleged debts exceeding £1,100, with threats of CCJs and no proper explanation of the charges.

The amount of stress, inconvenience, wasted time, and financial loss this has caused has been unbelievable. I have now lodged a formal complaint and intend to escalate this matter further with Ofgem and any other relevant bodies if necessary.

I would strongly advise others to stay well clear of Huddle, and those of you who have left 1 star reviews to escalate the matter further. Companies running like this should not exist.

I would like to share my experience so others don’t have to go through the same situation. This will be a bit long, but I want to give the full picture.

Before visiting, I looked through the reviews and noticed quite a few recent negative ones. I ignored them at the time, assuming people might just be overly picky. Based on that, I booked a viewing and test drive for a car I was interested in.

When I arrived, I waited around 30 minutes before a salesperson came to see me. While I was looking around the car, the salesperson stayed very close to me the whole time, constantly chatting. Looking back now, it almost felt like a distraction from properly inspecting the vehicle.

After the test drive, I noticed several issues with the car, including tracking problems, and it clearly was not prepared properly for sale from a cleanliness perspective either. Back at the desk, I said I would prefer to reserve the car and return once it was fully prepared before paying the full amount. The salesperson insisted that I had to pay in full that same day if I wanted the car, and said I could inspect it again on handover and receive a full refund if I was unhappy. I was also told this had to be done before 17:00 because the booking team would not be available afterwards. I disagreed, and eventually they accepted only a deposit, promising the car would be ready the following week.

On the handover day, I arrived at the agreed time of 15:00, but the car was still not ready. I was told it was “still being vacuumed,” which I accepted and waited patiently. Over the next three hours, I was given several different excuses, which I will spare in this review. Eventually, when I finally inspected the car, I found new scratches on the front that were not there during my first visit, along with warning errors showing on the dashboard.
The whole experience, along with the pressure-selling tactics, completely put me off purchasing the vehicle.
After cancelling the purchase, I then had to chase them several times by phone and wait a full week to receive my deposit refund.

It is also worth mentioning that during my first visit they pressured me to pay the full amount immediately because supposedly nobody from the finance team would be available later. However, on the handover day, they suddenly told me paying by card would have been absolutely fine.

Overall, I would strongly recommend avoiding this dealership if you can.

I rarely leave reviews, but I feel I need to share my experience due to serious concerns around communication and patient safety.

I am currently under this surgery for anticoagulation management, which requires careful monitoring. Over recent weeks, I have experienced repeated inconsistencies in information, poor communication, and a lack of clear clinical decision-making.

I was told to stop INR self-testing based on alleged hospital advice, however no written evidence or named clinician has ever been provided. The explanation for this has changed multiple times, including different reasons being given at different points, some of which do not align with the actual timeline of events.

Communication has been particularly poor. I have been told on several occasions that a GP would call me, but these calls have not happened. Instead, I have received text messages, which are not appropriate for discussing complex clinical situations. On one occasion, the issue was even marked as “no further action” without any proper discussion.

There have also been issues with appointment management. An INR test appointment that had been booked for nearly a week was changed without any notification, including a different time and clinician, which caused unnecessary confusion.

I was also told multiple times that my INR would be tested via a venous blood sample, however when I attended, it was done using a finger-prick machine—the same type used for home testing. This directly contradicts the reasoning given to me for stopping self-testing.

In addition, there have been problems with dosing and follow-up. On some occasions I have not been contacted with dosing instructions and have had to chase the surgery myself. I have also received unclear or inappropriate guidance from a GP regarding dosing, which is concerning given the risks associated with this medication.

Overall, I have been left without a clear, consistent plan for my care, and I do not feel confident in the communication or systems in place. Given the risks involved, I believe this surgery needs to review its processes to ensure safe and reliable patient care.
