one_star_reviews.text:
I visited Chole over a year ago for help correcting eyebrows that had been poorly done by another practitioner. They were asymmetrical, and my natural brow tails had been removed and replaced with PMU—something I had never requested and found very distressing.

Chole reassured me that she could improve the shape while keeping the result natural. I was very clear that I did not want darker or bold brows and was reassured this would not be the outcome. Based on this, I chose correction rather than full removal.

Although the shape was slightly improved, the brows healed much darker and more unnatural than I had wanted, which was exactly what I had hoped to avoid. I therefore chose not to proceed with the top-up appointment. At the time, I sent a polite message saying that overall she had done a good job but that I did not wish to continue, mentioning that I didn’t like the look of having no hair in the tails. In reality, my decision was due to the brows healing far bolder than I had asked for. Unfortunately, I did not receive a response.

More than a year later, I have now undergone my ninth removal session. Including the original treatment, I have spent around £1,000. This has been one of the most stressful and upsetting experiences I’ve had.

My advice to others would be to choose your practitioner very carefully and to seriously consider full removal rather than correction. I made the same mistake twice and paid for it—both emotionally and financially.

Update: At the start of the healing process, my brows did look improved overall, although I did feel they appeared extremely dark. I wasn’t too concerned at that stage, as I understood that brows typically lighten and soften significantly over the six-week healing period.

However, by the end of the six weeks, there was very little change. The colour didn’t fade as expected, and the brows still look overly saturated and blocky in appearance, which was extremely disappointing.

Chloe did explain that there were limitations to having my brows redone. However, my main concern was the risk of them becoming over-saturated. She reassured me that this would only happen after many sessions over a number of years, which made me feel comfortable proceeding.

Had I been made aware at any stage that the result could look overly saturated and blocky, I would not have gone ahead with the procedure.

The reason I didn’t contact Chloe immediately was because I first sought a consultation with a laser removal company. They advised that the discolouration above my brows, which I was concerned about, was actually residual ink still in the skin.
In contrast, Chloe suggested it was likely scarring and mentioned that she could offer a tattoo camouflage service to cover it, at an additional cost of £300. The laser clinic carried out a patch test, which successfully lifted the pigment completely.
This experience unfortunately made me lose confidence in Chloe’s assessment, as well as in her overall service and expertise.

I don’t believe this review is influenced by any wider issues; it is specifically based on my personal experience. My concern is that the service and advice provided did not resolve the initial problem and instead resulted in a worse overall outcome.

I am extremely disappointed with Appliance City and how they have handled what is clearly a serious fault.
I purchased a washing machine in November 2025 which has had a defective door from the very beginning. The door does not close properly, feels loose, and during operation it visibly moves in and out. Even more concerning, while the door is supposedly locked, it can be pulled open by approximately 2 cm. Under load, it leaks water from the bottom of the door and vibrates heavily during spin. This is not a minor issue or wear and tear—it is a fundamental failure of the door locking and sealing system on a relatively new appliance.
This has now become a genuine safety concern. I live in a household where both occupants are disabled—one is a wheelchair user and the other relies on walking sticks. Water leaking onto the floor creates a very real and dangerous slip hazard. An appliance that introduces that level of risk is clearly not fit for purpose, and it is deeply concerning that this has not been treated with urgency.
Despite clearly explaining the issue and providing video evidence, Appliance City have failed to take proper responsibility. Instead of addressing the problem as the retailer, they have repeatedly attempted to deflect the issue onto the manufacturer and hide behind internal processes, suggesting that nothing can be done without manufacturer involvement. This is simply incorrect and shows either a lack of understanding of consumer rights or a deliberate attempt to avoid dealing with the issue.
Communication has been slow and unhelpful, with a clear lack of urgency despite the safety implications. I have effectively been left chasing responses while dealing with a faulty and potentially unsafe appliance in my home.
For a product that was not cheap, and a fault that has been present since new, this level of service is unacceptable. When something goes wrong, you expect a company to step up and resolve it properly. In this case, Appliance City have done the opposite.
I would strongly advise others to think twice before purchasing from Appliance City. If something goes wrong, you may find yourself having to fight to get them to take even basic responsibility.

I visited Crazy Pedro’s (Bridge Street) on 22 January after seeing their widely advertised “£10 pizza” January offer.
When we arrived, the venue was very busy and, as is typical in winter, there was no outdoor seating. Inside is small with limited picnic bench-style seating, and there were no seats available. That said, we intended to order takeaway anyway.

Inside the venue, posters clearly advertised a number of pizzas for £10. Based on this, we ordered two pizzas expecting to pay £20.

At the point of ordering, we were then told that the £10 price only applied to dine-in customers and that takeaway orders incurred an additional £2.50 per pizza. This meant we paid £25 instead of £20 — a 25% increase on the advertised price, which was not made clear on the posters in-store.

This key condition was only explained at the counter, after we had already decided to order. The staff member serving us was polite and very apologetic, he advised that many other customers had raised the same issue, which suggests this was not an isolated case.

The Head of Brand and Marketing for the business has since confirmed that the in-store promotional material did not include the takeaway pricing. In practice, this meant the widely promoted “£10 offer” resulted in takeaway customers paying £12.50 (which is their standard price) so there was no actual saving at all.

What is most disappointing is how this has been handled. Despite the Head of Brand and Marketing clearly acknowledging in writing that the in-store information was incomplete, the response has been dismissive and has failed to address the core issue. Instead, a £5 voucher was offered (with conditions attached) which felt more like an attempt to drive repeat custom than a genuine effort to resolve the problem.

To add, this is not about £5 — it is about transparent pricing and trust. As local customers who live in Spinningfields and would typically visit regularly, we have not returned since as a direct result of this experience.

Crazy Pedro’s has lost two regular customers over what should have been a straightforward issue to resolve properly. If this is how they treat their customers, they don't deserve our business, let's go to one of the many other pizza places in town.

I was here for over 30 years No repairs of any kind, no fillings, no toothaches, negligible sensitivity and never used any sensitivity products.

On leaving my dentist Faheem Janjua's room after a checkup on 04/04/2024, he asked which hygienist I was seeing next. When I replied Saanya Idris, he twice stated, without giving reason, that I could have anyone I wanted.

Idris said that scrapes were old fashioned, and performed water jet cleaning. Then she changed her mind and performed a rough scrape as well. She slipped causing pain which nearly made me jump off the chair. Finally she rinsed my mouth repeatedly telling me to swallow until I had drunk about half a litre.

At home, I saw a puncture wound inside my cheek which had been bleeding. Over the next 36 hours various other pains escalated to an unbearable level.

I telephoned QRDC reception to change the hygienist for September. I heard an exclamation of panic, and the receptionist provided new bookings for almost the same times as the originals. She did not ask for my reason but recorded the change as "personal circumstance".

----
Ten days later I returned to see the dentist Nuwanthi Nanson about the pain, which I briefly described as cold sensitivity and widespread fluctuating toothaches.

She found several gum injuries, and suggested sensitive toothpaste. I had never used this so she instructed me. She proposed resin patches on my gums stating that they would fall off in two months, then changing this to five months. After agreeing, I asked directly whether they were permanent. She became angry and confirmed that they were. I changed my mind - this was a significant repair based on no knowledge of what actually happened: up to this point she had suppressed any conversation regarding the treatment given.

A quiet period had arrived, so I stated again that I had no problems before the recent treatment. She replied that it was "just co-incidence".

She asked how I brushed my teeth. I replied that I moved the Oral-B electric toothbrush in small circles while moving sideways. She stated that this was wrong and gave a lengthy tutorial: the brush should remain stationary on the tooth, letting the brush do the work, then lifting and moving to the next tooth. I remained silent throughout this. My long term brushing technique had never before caused any problem. Finally, she asked approximately three high level leading questions. I had given up and I was in pain and needed to leave, so I agreed to the built-in answers.

----
A week later, I was still in pain and now in distress. At this point there was no record at QRDC that I had been injured or was dissatisfied. I needed to have confidence that any dentist would be prepared to consider all the facts in order to determine what was wrong, so I wrote a letter to leave QRDC. This was my concluding statement:

".... I am writing to ensure that my complaint is properly recorded. I am not happy with the situation and am concerned about long term damage and pain. I am seeking help elsewhere and will no longer undergo any treatment by your practice, however kindly retain all previous records. I have cancelled the direct debit. I will not enter personally into any further discussion."

----
I received a letter from the hygienist Saanya Idris in which she stated she was not aware that I was experiencing any sensitivity and that if I told her then she would have changed her technique. There was no mention of her slipping causing wounds or of the bleeding.

As part of a full examination at a new dental practice, I was asked how I brushed my teeth. I replied exactly as I did at QRDC, and the dentist said that it was perfect.

I was subsequently referred to a dental surgeon who diagnosed nerve damage and recommended tricyclic medicine. Trauma was deferred on the basis that pain was widespread, not localised. No scan was taken.

I have used Amytriptyline, Pregabalin, Paroxetine and currently (November 2025) Nortriptyline, which all have serious side effects. At one point I stopped medication briefly but the pain escalated.

Overall the pains have been chronic headache, cold sensivity, toothache, and oddly also a feeling that teeth are loose and tender in the roots but only when closing my jaw.

----
Dental workers must be registered with the General Dental Council (GDC). The GDC's mission statement is to protect the public.

I made a complaint to the GDC. They confirmed receipt of material including the independant surgeon's report. The case was closed with no action. Included in the reasoning:

"sensitivity is a recognised symptom following scaling...it will normally subside after a few days".

"the care supplied to you was below the expected level for some aspects of the care, but the standard of practice was not unsatisfactory".

The hygienist Saanya Idris is still authorised to practice, GDC registration 312807, as can be found by searching the public register. She has a public linkedin profile (drsaanyaidris). The photo is many years out of date.

UPDATE MAY 2026:

The tricyclic medication was supposed to correct the chemistry between nerve signals and brain. But it had not helped, and the loss of coordination side effect was interfering with my sports and music activities. My GP changed the medication to 30/500 co-codamol to purely help with pain, taken every other day to prevent addiction. I also had a head MRI to investigate the constant headache (result pending). Amie failed to suspect the breech during 3 antenatal appointments, where she recorded the baby as head down. I should have been sent for a scan to check the presentation, but I wasn’t. But what is much worse, and what we only learnt later, is that Amie and her colleague should have been performing abdominal palpations during my labour to check the position of the baby. They did not do this even once. So not only did these midwives miss that the baby was breech – they were not even looking! Instead, they falsified these readings in the notes.

AMIE ALSO DISAPPEARED FROM MY HOMEBIRTH FOR 3 HOURS, just 1 hour after she had arrived. Not a word was said by either midwife about where she had gone or why. We later found out that AMIE HAD TAKEN HERSELF UPSTAIRS AND SLEPT IN OUR BED, WITHOUT OUR PERMISSION.

Amie and her colleague also ORDERED A MCDONALD’S TAKEAWAY TO OUR HOME DURING THE SECOND STAGE OF LABOUR. They knew I was feeling sick and that this was a major fear I had about birth, and they knew that I am vegan - but they ordered it anyway at 10:30 in the morning. They have since lied and said I gave them permission to do this. I did not.

The McDonald’s takeaway arrived during an obstetric emergency, just moments after the breech had been discovered. It was recommended I transfer to hospital for an emergency caesarean and me and my husband were told to go upstairs and decide what we wanted to do. This was despite the fact I had been downstairs for my entire labour. An emergency caesarean was my worst nightmare as I have a severe needle phobia, something which was discussed at length antenatally with Amie. Despite this, neither Amie or her colleague offered a single word of reassurance at this point. Neither Amie or her colleague gave us any information to enable us to make an informed decision. Me and my husband were then left upstairs scared and alone for 45 minutes whilst Amie and her colleague ate McDonald’s downstairs. They have since lied and said they came upstairs but did not want to disturb me as I was very upset. Not true – we left the bathroom door wide open. We did not want to be alone. They could not have come upstairs without our knowing it.

Despite neither Amie or her colleague caring for me during this time, there was a 17-MINUTE DELAY IN RINGING THE AMBULANCE. Amie and her colleague also tried to blame this on me and my husband, by saying that we told her not to ring one – another lie.

The baby’s heartrate was also not monitored properly in my labour. During the 2nd stage it should have been listened to at least once every 5 minutes (as per NICE guidelines). Amie and her colleague listened in on average just once every 29 minutes during my confirmed second stage. So, they should have been monitoring the heartrate 6 times as often as they were.

Even once the breech was discovered and they were dealing with an obstetric emergency, they did not monitor me or the baby properly. During this time, they left us completely unattended whilst they ate McDonald’s takeaway. My heartrate was also not monitored properly during labour. They did not check my blood pressure even once. They did not check my temperature even once. Instead, they falsified all of these readings. These are just some of the issues with the ‘care’ I received and some of the lies Amie has told since the birth. There are so many more that it would be impossible to fit them all into the space available for this review. We have reported Amie to the Nursing and Midwifery Council, who are currently investigating her fitness to practice as a midwife.

We booked Creature Comforts, Swadlincote to look after out home and pets during February 2019 half term.

They contacted us every evening to let us know that our pets were doing ok, giving the impression that they were actually spending time with them as agreed.

In reality,  Mr Bloor left at around 8am every day and returned at 7pm every evening.  He returned for just 4 minutes one day, 10 minutes the next and that pattern continued throughout the week.  The only time he exercised our three dogs was on the last day, where he stood at the back door and threw a toy for them ONCE.

Our dogs were bored and destructive, and we had informed them that our eldest boy had recently had a couple of minor strokes so we didn't like to leave him too long. He was left for long periods of time by this company who promised to care for our pets.

The cat litter was cleared out twice in six days (used by two cats), the chickens did not get cleaned,  fresh water or food topped up.

They had contacts in case of emergencies but did not inform them or us of their absence.  They only admitted to it when they were caught out by the fact our neighbours mentioned that the dogs were barking lots and they hadn't seen anyone at our house. After reviewing our CCTV we discovered that they hadn't been here.

The eldest two dogs became extremely ill the week after our return.  The resulting vet trips established that this is possibly due to a build up of toxins from eating the contents of the cat litter tray as they were left to do so each day.

We did our research and found this company on NARPS.  They came with all good reviews, insurance etc., however, it would seem that NARPS allow their customers to choose not to publish poor reviews if they dont want to.  It makes a mockery of the review process. NARPS have upheld our complaint against this company.

What should have been a much needed break has made us regret ever going away.  We are gutted that we left our animals in the care of this company, and have lost trust in anyone doing the job properly.  They let us down, and more I importantly they let our pets down.

Avoid: Substandard Cleaning & Appalling Aftercare

We hired this company for a professional clean last week and deeply regret it. To be transparent about our own situation when the cleaners finished, they were waiting outside the flat to leave, which meant we could only carry out a quick check on the spot. We trusted the company based on responses they typically leave on reviews, promising that any issues would be rectified. That trust was a mistake.

When our letting agency (Carter Jonas) carried out their full inspection, they identified a long list of missed items including limescale on multiple places, grease on the cooker hood and underside of kitchen units, dusty skirting boards in multiple rooms, debris on dining chairs, smeared mirrors, footprints in the shower tray, and hair left in the ensuite basin. Most shockingly, visible soiling was left on the toilet bowl something that should be the bare minimum of any cleaning job.

We provided photographic evidence of everything when asked, expecting the issues to be rectified promptly. Instead, Ali strung us along for days. He is consistently unresponsive to messages and only engages if you chase him by phone and even then, he promises callbacks that never come. He claimed he couldn't access emails due to "technical issues" and insisted on WhatsApp only. Right up until the agency's deadline, he kept assuring us someone would come to fix the job then changed his story at the last minute and refused to arrange anyone on the deadline day agency gave.

Even getting a basic invoice required multiple phone calls. Something that should take minutes became yet another exhausting chase.

As a result, we are now forced to pay a second cleaning company chosen by our agency to redo the work. We are pursuing a formal case against this company.

Do not hire them. The cleaning is substandard and, if anything goes wrong, the communication and accountability are even worse.

Staff were very respectful, and the health support workers in particular were especially lovely and helpful, but the centre itself does not seem equipped to deal with mastitis. Despite being a breast clinic, it felt focused on cancer care rather than on managing the most common condition affecting the breast in its primary function.

Breastfeeding is the core function of the breast and is essential for babies, yet there was little effort to support it. Mastitis was dismissed as a normal part of lactation, and the only advice offered was either to continue as normal or to stop breastfeeding altogether, rather than to properly assess and manage the issue.

There was no clear explanation of the condition, no interest or effort in considering current research, and antibiotics were used as a default despite not always being appropriate.

Furthermore, the advanced practitioner marked my breast with permanent marker for a scan, which I then had to scrub it off before I could feed my baby. This was difficult to remove, left my skin sore, and had to be done while my baby was crying for food, reinforcing the sense that the practical needs of breastfeeding patients are not being properly accounted for.

Overall, it is difficult to understand how a breast clinic can be so poorly set up to support or manage the most common condition affecting the breast in its primary function.

I’ve been a customer at Trotters Kensington for around 4 years and have always brought my 5-year-old son there for his haircut with the same hairdresser. Unfortunately, my latest experience was very disappointing.

We arrived 10 minutes late to our appointment because the bus was significantly delayed. We rushed to get there as quickly as possible, but as soon as we arrived, we were told we had to reschedule because their policy only allows a 5-minute delay.

I completely understand the importance of keeping appointments on schedule, and I appreciate that lateness can disrupt the day. However, at that moment the shop was not particularly busy, and given that we have been loyal customers for years, I was surprised there was no flexibility at all for what was clearly an exceptional situation.

On a previous occasion, I also had to wait 10–15 minutes myself before being served, so the lack of understanding this time felt quite disappointing.

I had actually planned to buy shoes in the store as well, but after the interaction I decided to leave. It was especially upsetting because my son was looking forward to the haircut.

A bit more empathy and customer care for long-term clients would have gone a long way.

Customer service is very uneven at this store. Have been shopping at Trotters at that particular location for over a decade. I will look at shopping online or at other locations than this one after today's experience and definitely would not recommend for their customer service.
